_meta.source: LINDDUN PRO Tutorial v0.1, Table 4.1 (Threat Type Mapping)
_meta.description: For each valid DFD interaction (source -- dataflow --> destination), the table indicates which LINDDUN threat types apply and at which position (S=source, fl=flow, D=destination). In the v0.1 tutorial every listed threat type applies at all three positions (S, fl, D) for every valid interaction. Invalid combinations (DataStore-flow-DataStore, ExternalEntity-flow-ExternalEntity) are excluded.
_meta.verified_against_source_pdf: 2026-07-07: fetched the tutorial PDF directly and confirmed page 18's Table 4.1 has exactly these 5 rows, no more -- this JSON is a complete, faithful transcription, not a gap. The page's caption reads verbatim: 'Note that invalid DFD element combinations (such as DataStore-flow-DataStore or ExternalEntity-flow-ExternalEntity) are not included in this table.' ExternalEntity->DataStore/DataStore->ExternalEntity are not named in that sentence but are equally absent from the table -- every one of the 5 valid rows has a Process on at least one side (the underlying rule: a DataStore is inert and an ExternalEntity is outside the system, so neither can meaningfully exchange data without a Process mediating). This matters a lot for the genomic scenario: NIST's own DFDs (SP 1800-43C) routinely show direct EntityStore/EntityEntity/StoreStore interactions (physical sample handoffs, direct freezer retrieval, in-person consultations) because NIST layers LINDDUN onto PANOPTIC, a broader framework that doesn't assume a mediating Process -- see WEEK3_REPORT.md's reachability finding (only 17/99 genomic threats sit on a Process-mediated interaction).

positions.fl: the data flow itself (data in transit)

invalid_interactions.reason: Data stores do not directly exchange data without a process.
External entities outside the system do not have modeled flows between each other.
